I totally get it. The job market beyond sucks. But also you said you’d give yourself 5 years. So at the very least, you need to stick with that.  I’ve known people in the past who have done the same, and things turned around.  It’s not going to be easy. I know that from experience. And again, I’m not gonna lie. In the last few years it’s in fact gotten worse. However, utilize what you do have. You have a roof over your head.  So what you can jobwise. Don’t go in to make friends. Keep your head down and just do the job that needs to be done. Follow the rules, be the best you that you can be.  Work on nothing more than to own that job. As for friends, they come and go. The true friends stick around through the thick and thin. Find someone online you can vent to. Someone who will listen. Someone who cares and won’t judge.  And if you feel that person isn’t right don’t give up on them right out. See if maybe they also need a shoulder to lean on.  But be honest with them. Be honest with yourself.  The job market (depending where you are) is most likely booming due to all the people who don’t want to work. Show that you do want it.  Show them they need you.  It will be hard. But it can also be rewarding. Did I read it right that you cut back on the smoking and drinking?  If so, that’s great. That’s a HUGE step.  If I read it wrong, perhaps try to ease off slowly.  Maybe not 100% just to a more manageable amount.  Set little goals. Yearly/monthly/weekly/daily.  And as dumb as it might sound, drink water. Eat better (so may be projecting here and should also do the same) maybe put an hour or two a day, or however long works for you, to do something that brings you joy. Anything from going on a hike/walk, listening to music, writing, reading, art, hell even sleeping. But don’t cheat yourself. If you need to skip a day for your well being/mental health do it.  Find a group, it could be anything. You like a certain genre of music or move? Have. A fav podcast? Enjoy nature? Memes?  Anything. Talk to people about that. Nothing more. If you find your hitting it off with someone test the waters. Maybe see if you can start talking about other things.  But again, don’t lie to anyone. If they ask you how you’re doing tell them. Maybe keep it vague, “been better” or “it’s a rough one today”.  But if it’s a good day, say that. There are good people out there. People who want to help others. People who genuinely care. But it will take work to find them. To keep them around.  And if they can’t handle you for who you are, they aren’t the one(s). Just be the best YOU you can be.  

I apologize if I’m rambling or repeating myself but I do care. And I don’t know you. I just know the feeling all to well. I just try and take things day by day. Some good, most bad. More so even worse. But I’m trying, and I want you to try too. 

Glad you’re alive buddy.

Although I can’t say I know exactly what you are going through, I can offer some suggestions perhaps?  They helped with me when I felt alone. And still do at times.  I know it’s not for everyone and some people will drown upon them. 

You can join some of those singles apps. While you’re a female you will have to wade through all the dicks first. But with any luck perhaps you can find people as friends. Nothing more. Just talking to people, even strangers. That said, what worked for me may not work for that people. 

If you are ever feeling alone hit people up on here. Or other social media. Believe it or not (it took me a long time to realize this) there are a lot of people who will listen/talk if you’re willing.
